entry.title: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization
entry.summary:
Text-to-image diffusion models can learn and reproduce an individual's identity from only a few reference photos, creating risks of unauthorized and misleading content generation. Proactive defenses address this risk by adding adversarial perturbations to facial images before release, thereby disrupting identity acquisition during downstream personalization. However, existing methods typically rely on dense $L_\infty$-bounded perturbations, whose accumulated distortions can become visible around facial structures.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #computer-vision #clean-tech

entry.title: Constructions of Efficiently Implementable Boolean Functions with Provable Nonlinearity/Resiliency/Algebraic Immunity Trade-Offs
entry.summary:
We describe new families of efficiently implementable Boolean functions achieving provable trade-offs between resiliency, nonlinearity, and algebraic immunity. Compared to one direction of research on balanced and 1-resilient functions with optimal algebraic immunity, the new functions provide lower algebraic immunity, but much lower -- in fact, almost optimal -- linear bias and importantly are much more efficient to implement. Compared to another direction of research based on constructions using direct sum, the new functions while achieving similar efficiency, has less number of variables for the same order of resiliency, same lower bound on algebraic immunity, and similar nonlinearity.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Authenticated Outsourced Incrementally Verifiable MPC
entry.summary:
Many privacy-preserving applications such as iterative machine learning training require executing ongoing computations over a secret state for long periods of time. While MPC enables secure computation, long-lived secret state is vulnerable to adaptive corruptions, requiring periodic share refreshes and committee rotation. In many settings, it is desirable for external parties to be able to verify that these state updates and rotations are performed correctly, but existing approaches for such public verifiability incur high overhead as they require MPC nodes to generate expensive proofs over secret-shared data.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems

entry.title: The Maximum Possible Nonlinearity for a Balanced Boolean Function in 10 Variables is 492
entry.summary:
Determining the maximum nonlinearity of 10-variable balanced Boolean functions has been a long-standing open problem. In this paper, we resolve it by proving that the maximum nonlinearity is exactly 492, thereby confirming Dobbertin’s conjecture in dimension 10. To exclude nonlinearity 494, we derive a quadratic residue for the Walsh spectrum and refine a local energy table from four-block concatenation by retaining the signs of the Walsh coefficients.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Cryptanalysis of Goldreich's PRGs with MAJ–XOR Predicates
entry.summary:
Goldreich's pseudorandom generators (PRGs) expand a secret $n$-bit seed into $m$ output bits by applying the same local predicate to each selected subset of seed bits. We develop a pooled recovery framework for $\mathrm{MAJ}$–$\mathrm{XOR}$ predicates. The method guesses that a set of seed bits has the same value and pools outputs whose majority inputs sufficiently overlap this set.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec

entry.title: A gentle introduction to lattice-based cryptography
entry.summary:
We present four quantum-safe schemes: the Kyber (ML-KEM) and FrodoKEM key encapsulation mechanisms, and the Dilithium (ML-DSA) and Falcon (FN-DSA) signature schemes. We also develop the mathematical background on lattices needed to understand why Kyber, FrodoKEM, Dilithium and Falcon are regarded as lattice-based cryptosystems, and we provide insight into the computational hardness of the underlying lattice problems. The exposition is intended to be accessible to senior undergraduate students and beginning graduate students.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: Constructions of Boolean Correctors with Optimal Nonlinearity and Vectorial Correctors Beyond Optimal Linear Correction Order
entry.summary:
Correctors are postprocessing functions that reduce or eliminate statistical bias in raw bitstreams produced by physical noise sources in true random number generators. In this paper, we develop a framework based on binary Krawtchouk polynomials for analyzing and constructing Boolean and vectorial correctors. This framework reformulates the Walsh-layer criterion into finite moment constraints on support-layer counts and preimage-layer counts.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
